title: Signature Lineage-Preserving Rewrite
description: Signature edition: every swarm rewrite carries the full lineage of the code it replaced — original author stamps, prior refactor history, and rationale — embedded as structured metadata in the new code. Nothing is ever rewritten anonymously; the archive can trace any line back through every swarm that touched it. This is a Signature original method.
method: Before replacing a node, the agent snapshots its lineage record; the new node embeds lineage: [prior ids, swarm run id, rationale]; the archive indexes lineage chains.
usage: Enable lineage capture in the swarm transform; query the archive to audit any line's full history.

title: Signature Tree-sitter incremental reparse
description: Signature edition: Tree-sitter parses code into concrete syntax trees incrementally — edits reparse only the changed region in microseconds. Refactoring swarms use it to keep a live, always-current structural index of huge codebases so every agent queries structure (not stale text) before rewriting.
method: One persistent parse tree per file; edits produce new trees reusing unchanged subtrees; queries (S-expressions) locate targets for the swarm.
usage: Maintain a tree-sitter index service; swarm agents query it for exact symbol locations before editing.

demo.code:
print('tree-sitter incremental parse:')
print('  edit line 42 -> reparse 1 node, reuse 999 subtrees')
print('  query (function_definition name: (identifier) @f) -> exact targets')

title: Signature Codemod canary with automatic revert
description: Signature edition: Before the swarm touches a million files, the transform runs on a canary slice (1% of files or one service). Metrics — test pass rate, diff size, review flags — decide whether to proceed, pause, or auto-revert the canary. Bad transforms die small instead of big.
method: Canary slice -> apply -> measure (tests, lint, diff stats) -> threshold check -> proceed or git revert the canary branch.
usage: Always canary first; encode the go/no-go thresholds in the swarm controller, not in anyone's head.

title: Signature Mutation testing of refactors
description: Signature edition: After the swarm rewrites code, mutation testing seeds small bugs (mutants) into the new code and checks the test suite kills them. If mutants survive, the tests are too weak to have validated the refactor — the swarm must strengthen tests before the change ships.
method: Generate mutants (operator swaps, constant changes); run the suite per mutant; kill-rate below threshold blocks the merge.
usage: Run mutation testing on refactored modules only (not the whole repo) to keep it fast; block merges under the kill-rate bar.

demo.code:
print('mutation testing gate:')
mutants = {'killed': 47, 'survived': 3}
rate = mutants['killed'] / sum(mutants.values())
print(f'  kill rate {rate:.0%} ->', 'PASS' if rate >= 0.9 else 'BLOCKED: strengthen tests')

title: Signature Cross-repo API migration bots
description: Signature edition: When a shared library changes its API, migration bots open pull requests in every consumer repo updating call sites to the new API. The swarm coordinates hundreds of such PRs, tracks their merge state, and escalates stuck ones — API evolution as a managed fleet operation.
method: Detect call sites via code search; generate per-repo patches; open PRs with the migration codemod; track merge state in a central board; escalate stale PRs.
usage: Freeze the new API first, generate patches per repo, and give owners a deadline before the old API is removed.

demo.code:
repos = ['svc-a', 'svc-b', 'svc-c']
for r in repos:
    print(f'  PR opened: {r} — migrate old_api() -> new_api() (codemod applied)')
print('migration board: 3 open, 0 merged, 0 stale')

title: Signature Refactor effect telemetry
description: Signature edition: The swarm instruments refactored code paths with telemetry — latency, error rate, call counts — and compares against pre-refactor baselines. A refactor that passes tests but doubles p99 latency is caught by telemetry, not by tests.
method: Baseline metrics snapshot before the wave; same dashboards after; statistical comparison ( Mann-Whitney or simple threshold bands); alert on regression.
usage: Snapshot baselines per wave, keep dashboards pinned during rollout, and wire alerts to the swarm controller.

demo.code:
before, after = 120, 132  # p99 ms
print(f'p99 latency: {before}ms -> {after}ms ({(after-before)/before:+.0%})')
print('verdict:', 'REGRESSION - flag wave' if after > before * 1.1 else 'within band')

title: Signature Semantic diff verification
description: Signature edition: Text diffs lie: reordered methods look like rewrites. Semantic diffing compares program meaning — normalized ASTs, control-flow graphs, or test behavior — so the swarm can prove a refactor changed structure without changing behavior, file by file, automatically.
method: Normalize both versions (sort members, strip formatting), compare ASTs modulo allowed transforms; run the file's tests before and after and require identical outcomes.
usage: Run semantic diff as a merge gate: any behavior change fails the shard automatically.

demo.code:
import ast
a = ast.dump(ast.parse('def f():
 return 1
'))
b = ast.dump(ast.parse('def f():

    return 1
'))
print('semantic diff:', 'IDENTICAL' if a == b else 'DIFFERENT', '(formatting ignored)')

title: Signature OpenRewrite recipe pipelines
description: Signature edition: OpenRewrite expresses refactors as composable recipes over a Lossless Semantic Tree (LST) that preserves formatting. Recipes chain (upgrade framework -> fix deprecations -> reformat), run across repositories, and produce verifiable diffs — the industrial version of swarm refactoring for the JVM ecosystem.
method: Recipes visit LST nodes with before/after templates; the engine runs recipes in order, auto-formats results, and reports changed files as a recipe run.
usage: Pick versioned recipes, run in a sandbox repo, review the recipe-run report, then apply fleet-wide.

demo.code:
print('OpenRewrite recipe run:')
recipes = ['org.openrewrite.java.spring.Boot2To3', 'org.openrewrite.java.Cleanup']
for r in recipes:
    print('  applied:', r)
print('  changed files: 1,204 — all diffs reviewable')

title: Signature Parallel git worktree shards
description: Signature edition: A swarm needs isolation: git worktrees give each agent its own checkout of the same repo at negligible cost (shared object store). Hundreds of agents refactor different directories concurrently, each committing to its own branch, and a coordinator merges the branches with conflict triage.
method: git worktree add per agent shard; agents commit to shard branches; coordinator merges in dependency order, re-running tests at each merge.
usage: Shard by top-level directory, cap agents per shard, and merge shards in topological order of module dependencies.

demo.code:
print('worktree shard plan:')
shards = ['auth/', 'billing/', 'search/']
for i, s in enumerate(shards):
    print(f'  agent-{i}: git worktree add ../w{i} -b shard/{s.strip("/")}')
print('3 isolated checkouts, one shared object store.')
